name: Marketing agency hero: dot-grid background with a cursor-tracked radial spotlight that lights up a brighter acid-green grid underneath
notes: Two identical dot-grid layers stacked: .grid-dim is always-visible at low opacity, .grid-bright is the same grid in acid-green clipped by a CSS mask-image radial-gradient centered on --spot-x/--spot-y — those two custom properties are updated on every pointermove via inline script (hero.style.setProperty), so the bright grid only shows in a ~260px circle around the cursor, like a flashlight over a PCB. No canvas, no per-frame JS loop — the mask just tracks the custom properties directly, so it's as cheap as a CSS transition. Under prefers-reduced-motion the script sets a fixed spot position once and never attaches the pointermove listener, so the bright patch just sits static near the headline instead of chasing a cursor that convention says shouldn't be implied. The floating .proof-card (client headshot + stat) is what stops this hero from reading as pure dev-tool aesthetic — don't drop it without replacing it with some other human/credibility element, or the section reads cold for a marketing (not SaaS) audience.
